IndiGo jumps nearly 5%, Asian Paints gains 2% as aviation, tyre, oil marketing stocks rally amid crude slump
IndiGo surged nearly 5 percent, while Asian Paints, Apollo Tyres and oil marketing stocks gained as Brent crude's nearly 25 percent plunge over 10 days lifted sentiment. Brent rebounded to $92.20 a barrel on Wednesday amid renewed Middle East tensions.
Shaleen Agrawal
November 11, 2026 / 10:23 IST
Crude oil price
IndiGo and paint stocks rallied on falling crude prices.
Brent crude dropped nearly 25 percent over 10 days.
Broader Indian markets surged with Sensex gaining 1.51 percent.

Shares of IndiGo, Asian Paints, Apollo Tyres and several oil marketing companies rallied on Wednesday, as a nearly 25 percent decline in Brent crude prices over the past 10 days boosted sentiment towards aviation, paint and tyre stocks. The gains came even as global oil prices recovered modestly from two-month lows amid renewed concerns over shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

InterGlobe Aviation, the parent company of IndiGo, surged 4.61 percent to Rs 5,680.10 in morning trade, emerging as the top gainer on the Nifty 50. Asian Paints climbed 2.18 percent to Rs 2,563.90 and was also among the leading Nifty gainers.
Apollo Tyres advanced 3.12 percent to Rs 428.20, while CEAT gained 1.57 percent to Rs 3,510. Berger Paints rose 1.09 percent to Rs 476.35, while Kansai Nerolac Paints and JK Tyre gained 0.55 percent and 0.52 percent, respectively.
Oil marketing companies also traded higher, with Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) rising 2.77 percent to Rs 396.45, Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) gaining 1.46 percent to Rs 320.60, and Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) advancing 0.71 percent to Rs 147.89.
Among upstream oil producers, Oil India declined 0.64 percent to Rs 436.20, while ONGC gained 0.59 percent to Rs 234.88. SpiceJet also edged higher, rising 0.26 percent to Rs 7.70.

Crude oil rebounds from two-month lows after 25% plunge
Global crude oil prices rose on Wednesday after falling to two-month lows in the previous session, as investors weighed hopes of de-escalation in the US-Iran war against concerns over continued attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures climbed 71 cents, or 0.78 percent, to $92.20 a barrel in early Asian trade, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 49 cents, or 0.57 percent, to $86.53.
The modest rebound followed a sharp selloff on Tuesday, when Brent briefly slipped below $90 a barrel and declined as much as 3.7 percent before settling below $92. Despite Wednesday's recovery, Brent has fallen nearly 25 percent over the past 10 days, reflecting a dramatic turnaround in the oil market.
The global benchmark remains almost 50 percent higher so far this year, but prices have retreated sharply from a six-month high amid expectations of reduced hostilities in the Middle East and continued growth in energy exports from the Persian Gulf.
Why are aviation, paint and tyre stocks gaining?
The steep correction in crude prices has improved the outlook for sectors that rely heavily on petroleum-based fuels and raw materials. For IndiGo, aviation turbine fuel is a major operating expense. A sustained decline in crude prices could translate into lower fuel costs, supporting operating margins and profitability.
Paint manufacturers such as Asian Paints, Berger Paints and Kansai Nerolac could benefit from reduced costs of petroleum-derived raw materials and solvents. Similarly, tyre manufacturers including Apollo Tyres, CEAT and JK Tyre could see relief in input costs, particularly synthetic rubber and carbon black.
The gains came amid a strong rally in the broader Indian market. At 10:05 am IST, the Sensex surged 1,221.31 points, or 1.51 percent, to 82,327.96, while the Nifty climbed 320.80 points, or 1.28 percent, to 25,365.45.
